In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the engagement smoothness of an actuated clutch depends on the clutch architecture, the frictional behavior of the facing materials, the engagement control strategy, and on the vehicle operating conditions.

the frictional characteristics of the clutch facing are a function of the pressure on them and of the sliding speed, and that the engagement performance of the clutch is affected by the frictional map of the clutch, which can be obtained through experimental tests.
the friction coefficient is a function of the pressure and sliding speed.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the frictional map is a key issue for the engagement control of an automated clutch.

the engagement performance of the dry clutch can be strongly improved by using the frictional map of the clutch, which is a function of the friction coefficient, the sliding velocity and the pressure, instead of the conventional map of the torque transmitted.

the engagement smoothness can be improved by the use of multi variable maps of the friction coefficient, and that the use of a reduced order model for the driveline can be an effective tool for control design.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the frictional map of the clutch is a key factor for improving the engagement quality and the control robustness.
the engagement smoothness of a clutch is strongly dependent on the frictional map, which in turn is influenced by several factors, such as the pressure, the sliding velocity and the temperature.
we can now model and simulate the engagement process in a way that is more realistic, and more useful, than ever before.
